subject: Risk & Compliance
title: Fatigue and Decision Errors
description: A quick, practical guide to Fatigue and Decision Errors.

hook.text: A trader works 18-hour shifts for two weeks straight. On day 14, she makes a $200 million pricing error.

buildup.text: Fatigue degrades decision-making, attention, and judgment — especially in high-pressure financial environments.

discovery.text: Medical studies show that working 24 hours impairs judgment as much as a 0.10% blood alcohol level.

twist.text: Finance celebrates overwork. The culture that demands 100-hour weeks creates the conditions for costly errors.

climax.text: Fatigue is a predictable operational risk. Managing work hours is a risk control, not a perk.

punchline.text: 18-hour days. Week two. Errors become inevitable.

quiz.question: How does fatigue affect decision-making?
options: 24 hours without sleep impairs judgment like alcohol intoxication
